full-text search for 'welch', 'ttest', 'ttest_ind', 't_test' and for the values 0.690 and 0.0031 across all roots
group_5_remaining.finding: No artifact stores a t statistic or p value for the from-scratch vs domain-pretrained gap on the clinical task. The figure survives only as prose in the C4 notebook's markdown header ('C37 found ... gap +0.0031, Welch p = 0.690'), in PHD_PLAN.md, CORRECTIONS.md, CONTRIBUTION.md and C44_PREREGISTRATION.md, which are exactly the unreliable source class. The C37 episode is attested in results/accord/control_cost_log.json only as a compute-cost line (compute_by_episode entry 'C37 clinical task, PubMedBERT vs scratch', gpu_minutes 612.3, runs 17), with no statistics. Two further caveats: results/accord/scaling/scaling_results.json holds the AG News public-data replication (three seeds per arm) but not the clinical comparison, and the notebook cell that computes the test calls scipy.stats.ttest_ind WITHOUT equal_var=False, so it is a Student test labelled Welch. Any recovered figure would need recomputation before it could be described as Welch.

group_5_remaining.name: public_text_over_calling_maximum_3.5
group_5_remaining.note: 3.50x is the maximum over-call ratio across the whole 3 models x 2 prompts x 4 prevalence levels grid on SNLI (public, non-clinical, human-labelled). The runner-up is 3.40x at the same model and prompt at 5 percent prevalence. This is the figure that contrasts with the 15.8x-23.6x clinical over-calling: it bounds how much of the clinical effect is attributable to asking an instruction-tuned model for a rare-class call rather than to clinical adjudication. Corroborated by the rendered table in the sibling REPORT.md, but the JSON above is the artifact.
